exposure: Laparoscopic lymph node evaluation (pelvic lymphadenectomy and/or sentinel lymph node mapping)
outcome: Obstetric outcomes (pregnancy, miscarriage, mode of delivery)
cohort: 31 women aged <45 years with low-risk cervical cancer (stage IA1 with positive lymphovascular space invasion, stage IA2, or stage IB1 ≤2 cm with <10 mm cervical stromal invasion) who underwent fertility-preserving treatment.
finding: Cervical conization with lymph node assessment by sentinel lymph node mapping/lymphadenectomy is an oncologically safe procedure in patients with low-risk cervical cancer, with no recurrences detected after a median follow-up of 41.4 months and successful pregnancies achieved in a majority of those who attempted.
